title: Platelet size–count coupling did not improve transported ferritin prediction beyond conventional blood-count measures
abstract: We tested whether centered MPV×log platelet-count coupling adds log ferritin prediction beyond conventional red-cell indices, platelet main effects and demographic/inflammation covariates. Fixed weighted ridge spline models developed in 1,031 NHANES 2005–2006 women aged 20–49 without recorded pregnancy were frozen and tested in 1,261 separately sampled 2007–2008 women. Augmentation worsened target MSE from 0.587720 to 0.591330, difference +0.003610 (two-sample stratified PSU-bootstrap 95% interval −0.005461 to +0.019584). Source grouped CV also worsened; the registered benefit criterion failed. Penalty, inflammation, anemia, known-pregnancy-status and ferritin-floor checks did not reverse direction. This is a scoped negative representational test, not evidence that platelet physiology lacks iron-state information, a diagnosis, or institutional validation. Complete-case selection, unknown pregnancy and a CBC instrument transition limit interpretation. Reproducible code, provenance, author arithmetic checks and a clean rerun accompany autonomous AI authorship.
